21645374.QUESTION: Do statins reduce all-cause mortality in elderly patients with coronary artery disease?
CONTEXTS: Statins are widely prescribed for primary and secondary cardiovascular prevention, but their efficacy in elderly cohorts remains debated.
A prospective cohort study of 4,200 patients aged 75 and older with documented coronary artery disease was conducted over a 5-year follow-up period.
Statin therapy was associated with a 24% reduction in all-cause mortality (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.65-0.89, p < 0.001) compared to non-users.
21645374.LONG_ANSWER: Statin treatment significantly reduces all-cause mortality in elderly individuals with established coronary disease.

22341908.QUESTION: Does routine antibiotic prophylaxis decrease postoperative infection rates in clean elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy?
CONTEXTS: Elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy is one of the most common clean-contaminated surgical interventions.
A randomized controlled trial compared single-dose cephalosporin vs placebo in 1,000 low-risk elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy cases.
Surgical site infection rates were 1.8% in the antibiotic group versus 1.9% in the control group (p = 0.89), demonstrating no clinical benefit.
22341908.LONG_ANSWER: Routine antibiotic prophylaxis does not decrease postoperative infectious complications in low-risk clean elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy.

23456789.QUESTION: Can serum biomarker panel accurately differentiate benign from malignant pulmonary nodules smaller than 8 mm?
CONTEXTS: Indeterminate solitary pulmonary nodules under 8 mm pose diagnostic challenges in low-dose CT lung cancer screening.
We evaluated a 5-protein autoantibody panel across 350 patient serum samples with solid nodules ranging from 4 to 8 mm.
The diagnostic panel yielded 78% sensitivity and 62% specificity, showing diagnostic potential but insufficient standalone specificity for clinical staging.
23456789.LONG_ANSWER: The serum biomarker panel shows modest discriminatory ability but evidence remains inconclusive for definitive clinical replacement of serial imaging.
